curated.summary: Section 6: Revocation how made.—A proposal is revoked—
curated.plain_english: (1) by the communication of notice of revocation by the proposer to the other party; (2) by the lapse of the time prescribed in such proposal for its acceptance, or, if no time is so prescribed, by the lapse of a reasonable time, without communication of the acceptance; (3) by the failure of the acceptor to fulfil a condition precedent to acceptance; or (4) by the death or insanity of the proposer, if the fact of his death or insanity comes to the knowledge of the acceptor before acceptance.

curated.plain_english: must— (1) be absolute and unqualified; (2) be expressed in some usual and reasonable manner, unless the proposal prescribes the manner in which it is to be accepted. curated.plain_english: conditions of a proposal, or the acceptance of any consideration for a reciprocal promise which may be offered with a proposal, is an acceptance of the proposal.

curated.summary: Section 9: Promises, express and implied.—In so far as the proposal or acceptance of any promise is made
curated.plain_english: in words, the promise is said to be express. In so far as such proposal or acceptance is made otherwise than in words, the promise is said to be implied. 12 OF CONTRACTS, VOIDABLE CONTRACTS AND VOID AGREEMENTS

curated.summary: Section 10: What agreements are contracts.—All agreements are contracts if they are made by the free
curated.plain_english: consent of parties competent to contract, for a lawful consideration and with a lawful object, and are not hereby expressly declared to be void. Nothing herein contained shall affect any law in force in 1[India] and not hereby expressly repealed by which any contract is required to be made in writing2 or in the presence of witnesses, or any law relating to the registration of documents.

curated.summary: Section 11: Who are competent to contract.—Every person is competent to contract who is of the age of
curated.plain_english: majority according to the law to which he is subject3, and who is of sound mind, and is not disqualified from contracting by any law to which he is subject.

curated.summary: Section 12: What is a sound mind for the purposes of contracting.—A person is said to be of sound mind
curated.plain_english: for the purpose of making a contract, if, at the time when he makes it, he is capable of understanding it and of forming a rational judgment as to its effect upon his interests. A person who is usually of unsound mind, but occasionally of sound mind, may make a contract when he is of sound mind. A person who is usually of sound mind, but occasionally of unsound mind, may not make a contract when he is of unsound mind. curated.plain_english: held exclusively liable.—When a person who has made a contract with an agent induces the agent to act upon the belief that the principal only will be held liable, or induces the principal to act upon the belief that the agent only will be held liable, he cannot afterwards hold liable the agent or principal respectively.
